blocks.x: A working build of Cyber & Zero-Trust inside Logistics & Supply Chain: the operating context that shapes it, the services sequenced through the method, and the deltas we commit to.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Double-brokering fraud and carrier-identity theft rise alongside ransomware targeting 3PLs; the estate mixes corporate IT with driver-facing OT.
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower make up the delivery pattern — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — run through the Dataq Method with GDPR obligations baked into the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Carrier identity verification and double-brokering detection analytics (fraud losses down measurably)
Segmentation between corporate IT and operational systems with recovery drills (operations continue through IT events)
Hours instead of days via agentic remediation
Intercepted in transit, not at claims

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GDPR and GDPR. Driver and customer data duties across telematics. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

A fixed rhythm keeps progress visible from week one — here is the one we run. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
